text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @Alice (oncall) and @Sandeep — GPU cluster saturation detected in us-west-2. Autoscaler not recovering, high queue growth, customer-facing 429s reported. Alert ID 2026-aws-gpu-sat-1799991234

Alice (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing dashboard links, can someone post the scale group status?

Raj: looking now — autoscaler logs show repeated `ScaleUpRejected: capacity-limit` for pool gpu-hotpath-1. Also seeing a spiky influx from a single API key (cs-frontend-prod).

Maria: cpu/gpu metrics: GPU util ~98% for last 6m, pending queue length growing from 200 -> 1.2k in 15m. Token-bucket rejects spiking, hitting 429s from gateway.

Jess: Support reporting major UX degradations for 2 customers (Acct A, Acct B). Customer Success pinged Elena.

Customer Success - Elena: Confirmed customers saw intermittent 429s since ~12:10 UTC. They're seeing retries and elevated latencies, some timed out.

Tom: Noted that a recent tier-policy change rolled out last night tightened burst allowances for Dedicated tiers. Could be correlated. Who owns token-bucket config?

Raj: Token-bucket service (rate-policy) owner is eng-platform. The policy that changed is `tier-burst-window` — reduction from 3s->1s for non-SLA tiers. I see the config pushed at 03:45 UTC (deploy-bot shows 1799900000).

Maria: Adding logs from head node: ```
[autoscaler] 12:22:10 ScaleUpRejected: regionQuotaExceeded, requested 8 GPUs, available 2
[autoscaler] 12:22:52 ScaleUpRejected: policyCooldownActive
[kube-proxy] 12:23:05 PodEviction: draining delayed -> backlog++
```

Alice (oncall): So we have three contributing issues: capacity quota (cloud), cooldown/policy preventing scale, and a stricter token-bucket making API-layer 429s. Prioritize mitigation: immediate customer-impact reduction. Ideas: 1) emergency increase quota/evict lower-priority workloads 2) temporarily relax token-bucket burst window for affected tiers 3) enable regional failover for a subset of traffic 4) manual scale if cloud permits.

Sandeep: I can open an emergency support case with cloud (US-West GPU quota). Meanwhile we can disable the recent tier policy rollout for rate-policy service. Rolling back the patch is fastest.

Raj: We can also reduce per-tenant concurrency for non-SLA customers at the routing layer to free up slots for SLA customers. I can flip a routing flag.

Maria: If we reduce concurrency limits, queue will still grow but we can preserve throughput for high-tier. Recommend applying selective throttling for non-SLA keys and bump the token-bucket burst for SLA keys to 2x.

Jess: Prioritize Acct A/B (they're SLA). We should add them to the whitelist for emergency higher burst. I can produce the list.

Alice (oncall): Actions: A) @Sandeep open cloud quota ticket and request temporary quota raise. B) @Maria rollback rate-policy deploy for `tier-burst-window` or patch to original values. C) @Raj apply routing flag `preserve-sla-concurrency=true` and lower default concurrency to 6. D) @Jess build whitelist for SLA customers and post keys. E) I'll coordinate customer comms and update channel every 10m.

Sandeep: Cloud case opened: INC-981234, requested +20 GPUs while we investigate. ETA unknown but escalated. (Case ref in ticketing).

Maria: Rolling back rate-policy now. Command: ```bash
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/rate-policy-service --to-revision=172
```
Rolling back — observing config change propagation.

DeployBot: Rollout undo started for rate-policy-service. Revision 172 -> in_progress.

Raj: Applying routing flag: ```json
{ "preserve_sla_concurrency": true, "default_concurrency": 6 }
```
Flag flip committed to feature-gates. Propagating to edge routers.

Maria: Rate-policy rollback completed, previous burst-window restored. Monitoring token-bucket rejects...

Maria: Token-bucket rejects dropped ~60% in 2m. 429 rate at gateway decreased accordingly. Good signal.

Alice (oncall): Good. How's queue length?

Maria: Queue peaked ~1.2k, now dropping to ~400 after rate-policy rollback + routing flag. GPU util still high but stabilizing.

Beside recovery steps — we need to fix autoscaler failing to scale earlier. Raj, can you surface autoscaler logs for the cooldown/policy errors?

Raj: Found autoscaler mis-evaluating pending pods as unschedulable due to nodeSelector mismatch after yesterday's runtime change. A stale nodeSelector (`runtime: v1-legacy`) was added to hotpath PodTemplate. That prevented new nodes from being considered compatible -> scale rejected by scheduler. Patch available.

Alice (oncall): Oof. So runtime rollout caused mismatch, autoscaler attempted to create nodes but scheduler rejected pods, leading to ScaleUpRejected loops?

Raj: Exactly. Fix is to revert PodTemplate or patch nodeSelector to include `v1-legacy` label on new nodes. I'm prepping a patch to PodTemplate to remove nodeSelector. Will run as hotfix.

Maria: If we fix PodTemplate and cloud grants GPUs, autoscaler should scale normally. But we need to be careful with in-flight priority.

Tom: Postmortem note: the tier-policy change + runtime nodeSelector change were both in last 24h — these interacting changes created a perfect storm. We should consider gating infra and policy changes together for hotpath.

Raj: Hotfix applied to PodTemplate: `kubectl apply -f podpatch.yaml` -> removed nodeSelector. New pods scheduling onto pending nodes now. Watch logs: ```
[kube-scheduler] 12:38:33 Binding pod/req-xxx -> node/gpu-78
```

DeployBot: Hotfix deployment succeeded.

Alice (oncall): After hotfix + rate-policy rollback + routing flag, customer 429s reduced to negligible, queue draining. GPU util falling to ~70% over next 10m.

Jess: Notifying Acct A/B with interim update: we mitigated the root cause, we're monitoring, next update in 30m. :thumbsup:

Customer Success - Elena: Customers acknowledged update, asked for RCA and ETA for full recovery.

Sandeep: Cloud replied — temporary quota increase approved for 4 GPUs; still below requested but helps absorb burst while autoscaler recovers.

Alice (oncall): Current status: degraded -> recovering. Remaining work: 1) full cloud quota resolution 2) postmortem and revert process for the two configs 3) add safety gate to prevent simultaneous infra+policy rollouts 4) token-bucket tuning automation to avoid tight bursts during saturation.

Tom: I'll schedule a postmortem meeting and own the action items for rollout gating with eng-platform + eng-runtime.

Raj: Action items I own: audit PodTemplates across hotpath, add autoscaler integration tests for nodeSelector compatibility, add alert for `ScaleUpRejected: policyCooldownActive` frequency.

Maria: Action items I own: add dashboards for token-bucket rejects by tier, automatic rollback trigger when 429s > 5% for 3m after policy change.

Jess: I'll follow up on customer comms and collect impact windows for billing/credits.

Alice (oncall): Great work everyone. I'll close the incident once metrics are stable for 30m and customer comms are sent. Logging final note: incident-bot updated incident severity to SEV2 -> monitoring for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident 1799991234 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pages: 8, SLO impact window: 12:09-12:46 UTC.

--- End of thread ---
